items.claim: The test 'creates new stack if original error has no stack' now passes `new Error('original')`, which has a stack, so it no longer exercises the no-stack branch it is named for.
items.consequence: The old `{ message: 'original' }` reached the `else if (Error.captureStackTrace)` fallback in GraphQLError.js (lines 201-209) with an originalError present; the new input takes the `originalError.stack` branch, duplicating the previous test. A regression that leaves `stack` undefined for a stack-less original error (e.g. a cross-realm or `Object.create(Error.prototype)` error) would still pass. Deleting `original.stack` after construction, or a cast object, would keep the coverage.

items.claim: Only the `declare class` constructor was widened to accept `null` for `nodes`; the implementation's signature still says `$ReadOnlyArray<ASTNode> | ASTNode | void`.
items.consequence: Callers are checked against the declaration and may now pass `null`, while Flow checks the body as if `nodes` is never null. It works today only because the body uses truthiness checks; a later refactor to `nodes !== undefined ? [nodes] : undefined` would type-check and yield `[null]`, then crash on `node.loc` for the `new GraphQLError('msg', null, ...)` calls used throughout the tests and `locatedError`.

items.claim: The 'serializes to include message and locations' test no longer builds its node from `parse('{ field }')`, so the single-line, string-input location case is dropped from this file.
items.consequence: Every node-derived location assertion in the file now uses the same node (line 2, column 3, position 4) from one shared `Source`. A regression in `getLocation` for first-line positions other than offset 0, or for sources created implicitly from a string, is no longer caught here; the old expectation `{line:1,column:3}` was the only such case.

items.claim: The no-argument construction `new GraphQLError()` was replaced by `new GraphQLError('str')` to satisfy Flow, removing the only check that the constructor tolerates a missing message.
items.consequence: Untyped JS consumers can still call `new GraphQLError()`. If the constructor later starts dereferencing `message` (e.g. `message.trim()`), it would throw a TypeError for them and no test would catch it.

items.claim: A bare `// $FlowFixMe` with no explanation suppresses any Flow error on the next line just to keep a `String.raw` tagged template.
items.consequence: The suppression hides every Flow error on that line, including a future wrong-typed call to `inspect` or `expect`, and gives no reason or issue link, unlike the `$FlowFixMe workaround for: <issue>` comments in src/jsutils. Writing the expected value as the plain literal `'"\\""'` needs no suppression.

items.claim: Annotating the fixtures as `e: any` turns off type checking for the `locatedError(e, [], [])` calls these tests exist to exercise, despite the file being marked `@flow strict`.
items.consequence: If `locatedError`'s `originalError` parameter type is narrowed or changed, the two tests at lines 29 and 41 still type-check because `any` flows into the call. Keeping `e` typed as `Error` and adding the extra properties via `Object.assign` or a cast at the assignment only would preserve the check.

items.claim: Fixture parsing and `invariant` calls were hoisted to module top level, so they run at import time instead of inside a test or `before` hook.
items.consequence: If `parse` or `dedent` regresses, or an invariant fails, the exception is thrown while mocha loads the file. That aborts the whole run with a load error instead of reporting the affected `it` blocks as failed, and tests in other files do not run.

items.claim: The new locals `opA`/`opB` hold object type definitions, not operations, and the narrowing block is copy-pasted for A and B with a further combined `invariant(fieldA && fieldB)`.
items.consequence: Maintainability cost only: the `op` prefix suggests OperationDefinition nodes, mirroring `operationNode` in the sibling test, and the same three-line parse/invariant/`fields[0]` sequence is duplicated. A small local helper returning the first field's type, or names like `typeDefA`, would remove both the duplication and the misleading name.
